text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday.
- Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa meets tourist workers in the resorts of Makarska and Korcula on the southern Adriatic coast and promises them assistance in preparing the tourist season.
- Croatia is expecting some 520,000 Slovene visitors in summer of 1997, says assistant tourism minister and head of the Croatian Tourist Association Marijan Bulat.

- Goran Hadzic, Slavko Dokmanovic and Milos Stanimirovic top the list of suspected Serb war criminals compiled by the Croatian government and handed over to the Serb side by transitional administrator of Eastern Slavonia Jacques Klein.
- The exhumation of some 70 Croats from a mass grave begins in Bacin near Hrvatska Dubica in central Croatia.
- Gross Domestic Product (GDP) officially estimated to have risen 6.4 percent in the third quarter of 1996 compared to the same period of 1995.
- Banking news: Splitska Banka to sell its stakes in firms obtained in debt-for-equity swaps for uncollected loans.
- Foreign Minister Mate Granic visits Poland, a large prospective market for Croatian goods.
- Commentary: Croatian exports to dollar markets account for only 18.7 percent of the total. Who is gaining and who is losing due to the dollar strength?
- Croatia and Macedonia prepare a free trade agreement. Industrial products to be exempt of customs duties immediately.
- Economy Ministry announces stricter quality controls to prevent poor quality goods being imported.

- Banking news: Agroobrtnicka Banka expects a new 10 million German marks credit line from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development after disbursing the first such loan to farming and other small enterprises.
- Zagreb statistics: January wages only slightly higher than a month earlier but living costs rose at a quicker pace.
- Belgrade requests dual Croatian-Yugoslav citizenship for Eastern Slavonia Serbs but Yugoslav constitution does entitle Croats in Voivodina and Kosovo Albanians to the same right.
- There is no peaceful solution for Bosnia and Herzegovina, says Bruce Pirnie, a long-time military analyst at American intelligence agency DIA.
- Stock market: Zagrebacka Banka ordinary shares accounted for almost a half of last week's 21.8 million kuna trade. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
